evidence: The runtime builds operation-specific target choices and sends operation plus all target heads in one System One request.
A separate OpenAI-compatible helper generates JSON text only for fill operations.
The loop predicts, consumes a decision once, executes, observes again, and terminates on DONE or BLOCKED.
One browser-side evaluation extracts visible controls, text, stable node identities, guards, and bounded actions.
Execution rechecks freshness, visibility, geometry and occlusion before dispatching CDP input.
The documented MVP excludes frames, shadow roots, canvas, uploads, pop-ups, nested scrolling, and complex keyboard interactions.
The matched six-run report records a 25 percent median reduction on one Flights task and explicitly rejects broad generalization.
The Flights example verifies route, trip type, date and visible results independently of the model's DONE choice.
TypeSafe documents many questions in one request and parallel evaluation with code selecting relevant answers.
Choice is limited to caller-defined criteria and returns a full probability distribution.
Jev 1.13 is text-only; non-text inputs must be preprocessed into text or structured state.
A public issue reports omitted non-native autocomplete rows causing repeated fills until the action budget was exhausted.
